rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a multimodal configuration with established encoders (scvi_n200 for RNA, imagenet_vit_l for images) and aggregation/fusion methods (avgpool, weighted). It clarifies whether combining RNA and image data improves accuracy, addressing the core hypothesis of multimodal profiling. This is the best use of the first experiment to set a baseline for comparison.

The existing evidence shows that the multimodal multiprofile setup with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l achieves 0.706 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation, which could capture more complex interactions between modalities. It directly builds on the previous configuration's successful multimodal setup while exploring a key design choice (aggregation method) that may significantly impact performance.

Existing evidence shows config_012 (0.725 accuracy) is the best so far. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder (resnet50 vs. imagenet_vit_l) while keeping RNA encoder (scvi_n200), aggregation (transformer), and fusion (weighted) consistent. This clarifies whether the image encoder choice impacts performance, building on config_012's strong foundation. It balances exploitation (using proven components) and exploration (testing alternative image encoders).

The existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_012) yield the highest accuracy so far (0.725). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 → scgpt) while keeping the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation (transformer), and fusion (weighted) consistent. This clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice impacts performance in this effective setup, balancing exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of alternative encoders.

The existing evidence shows config_012 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) has the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders and aggregation method but uses concat fusion instead of weighted fusion. This clarifies whether the fusion method choice is critical, balancing exploitation of the current top setup with exploration of alternative designs.

The existing evidence shows config_012 (0.725 accuracy) is the top performer with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 → pca_n2000) while keeping other components identical, clarifying if RNA encoder choice significantly impacts performance. It balances exploration of key design choices (RNA encoder) with exploitation of proven effective components (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion).

The existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_012: 0.724989) is highly effective. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 → pca_n2000) and image encoder (imagenet_vit_l → resnet50) while retaining the high-performing transformer and weighted setup. This clarifies whether the RNA/image encoder choices are critical for further gains, balancing exploration of new encoder combinations with exploitation of proven aggregation/fusion methods.

Existing evidence shows config_012 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to resnet50 image encoder and concat fusion (vs. weighted fusion) could improve performance, while keeping scvi_n200 RNA encoder and transformer aggregation. It balances exploration of image encoder choices with exploitation of the current best aggregation method.

The existing evidence shows config_012 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests avgpool aggregation and concat fusion with the same RNA/image encoders (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l), which could clarify if these parameters are optimal. It balances exploitation (using proven encoders) and exploration (testing aggregation/fusion variants) to maximize the chance of improving upon the current best.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_012) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests changing the image encoder to resnet50 and aggregation to avgpool while retaining scvi_n200 RNA and weighted fusion, which could clarify if these changes impact performance. It balances exploration of image encoder alternatives with exploitation of the top-performing RNA and fusion choices.
